title: Getting Started
description: Steps to begin using the Blood Bank system.
content:
## Getting Started

This section helps new users begin using the Blood Bank system in a simple and structured way. It explains the basic steps to access the application, understand the main screens, and start working with the core workflows.

### Before You Start

Before using the system, make sure you have the required access and basic information ready.

- Log in with your assigned username and password.
- Confirm that your account has the correct access for the tasks you need to perform.
- Keep donor details, collection information, and storage details ready if you are entering new blood units.

### First Login

When you open the Blood Bank application for the first time, you will be taken to the main dashboard after login.

- The dashboard gives a quick overview of the current system status.
- You can use the sidebar or menu to move between modules.
- Each module contains its own set of screens for managing related tasks.

### Understanding the Main Areas

The system is divided into modules so users can work in a clear and organized way.

- Dashboard provides a summary view of blood availability and operational counts.
- Donor module is used for donor registration, editing, and donor details.
- Inventory module is used for blood unit tracking, storage, and status handling.
- Lab Testing module is used for screening and test result updates.
- Settings and master data modules are used to manage supporting reference values.

### Typical Work Sequence

A typical Blood Bank workflow usually follows this order.

- Register or identify the donor or source.
- Add the blood unit into the system.
- Assign QR tracking if required.
- Complete screening or testing.
- Store the unit in the correct location.
- Handle reservation, issue, return, transfer, or discard when needed.

### How to Use the System Effectively

To work smoothly in the system, follow a few simple practices.

- Always verify the donor or source before creating a blood unit.
- Enter storage details correctly so the unit can be found later.
- Check the unit status before performing any action such as reserve, issue, or discard.
- Review the timeline or history when you need to understand what happened to a unit.

### Helpful Notes for New Users

A few screens may look similar, but they serve different operational purposes.

- Inventory is for active blood unit tracking.
- Lab Testing is for screening and result handling.
- Discarded or expired units are handled separately from active stock.
- QR-based lookup makes it easier to identify and manage a unit quickly.

### Next Steps

Once you are familiar with the basic navigation, you can move into the main modules and start using the system for daily operations.

- Learn how donor records are managed.
- Learn how blood units are added and tracked.
- Learn how screening, storage, and movement workflows work.
- Review the settings and master data used throughout the system.

This guide gives you the basic starting point. The next sections explain each module in more detail so you can use the system confidently in day-to-day blood bank operations.

title: Introduction
description: Overview of the Blood Bank system and its main purpose.
content:
## Overview

Blood Bank is a centralized blood bank management system designed to help staff manage donor records, blood collection, screening, inventory, storage, issue handling, returns, discard flow, and related operational activities in one place.

The system is built to support the complete lifecycle of a blood unit, from the moment a donor is registered or a unit is received from another source, until the unit is screened, stored, issued, returned, discarded, or moved between storage locations. It helps teams maintain accurate records, reduce manual tracking, and manage blood bank operations in a structured and reliable way.

### What the system helps with

Blood Bank provides a clear workflow for handling daily operational tasks such as:

- managing donor details and contact information
- adding blood units from collection or external sources
- tracking screening and testing progress
- storing units in the correct location
- monitoring unit status and movement history
- reserving, issuing, returning, or discarding blood units
- reviewing inventory summaries and blood group availability

### Why it is useful

Blood bank operations require accurate tracking, fast access to information, and careful handling of every blood unit. This system helps teams keep all important information connected in one place so users can work faster, avoid duplicate records, and follow the correct process at every stage.

### Who uses it

The application is intended for blood bank staff who handle:

- donor management
- collection and inventory updates
- laboratory screening
- storage and movement of blood units
- issue and return operations
- reporting and daily operational review

### High-level workflow

In a typical flow, a blood unit is collected or received, linked to the relevant donor or source, assigned a QR code, screened in the laboratory, and then moved into the appropriate storage location. From there, it can later be reserved, issued, returned, transferred, or discarded based on the actual operational status of the unit.

This documentation explains the Blood Bank system from an end-user perspective and focuses on how to use the available screens and workflows effectively.

title: Key Features
description: Main capabilities of the Blood Bank system.
content:
## Key Features

### Donor Management
- Add and manage donor records in a structured way.
- Store donor profile details, contact information, blood group, and related history.
- Track donor-related activities across the system.

### Blood Collection and QR Tracking
- Register blood units collected from donors or received from other sources.
- Assign QR codes to blood units for easy identification and tracking.
- Use QR-based lookup to manage units quickly and accurately.

### Inventory and Storage Management
- Track available blood units across different blood groups.
- Store units in the correct building, zone, and equipment.
- View current stock, storage status, and unit movement clearly.

### Lab Testing and Screening
- Record mandatory screening results for blood units.
- Monitor whether tests are pending, in progress, safe, or failed.
- Move units through the correct screening and storage workflow.

### Reservation, Issue, and Return
- Reserve blood units for patient requirements.
- Issue units when needed and track issue history.
- Handle returned units and re-testing before reuse.

### Discard and Expiry Handling
- Identify expired, failed, damaged, or unusable blood units.
- Move such units into discard flow with proper reason tracking.
- Keep discarded units separate from active inventory.

### Communication and Follow-Up
- Maintain donor communication history in one place.
- Track phone follow-ups, responses, and remarks.
- Support better donor engagement and re-contact workflows.

### Settings and Master Data
- Manage supporting records such as locations, reasons, and storage data.
- Keep system values configurable from one place.
- Use master data across different workflows consistently.

### Dashboard and Reporting
- View quick summaries of blood stock and unit status.
- Check key counts and operational visibility from dashboard views.
- Use reports for day-to-day monitoring and review.

title: Workflow at a Glance
description: A clear overview of the Blood Bank operational workflow.
content:
## Workflow at a Glance

Blood Bank follows a clear operational flow so staff can manage donor data, blood units, screening, storage, and blood movement in a structured way. The system is designed to keep each step connected so users can easily understand where a blood unit came from, what happened to it, and where it is currently stored.

### 1. Donor or Source Identification

The workflow begins when a blood unit is created from an internal donor collection or received from an external blood bank.

- Internal collection is linked to a donor record.
- External blood units are linked to the source blood bank and external reference details.
- The system captures the basic information needed to track the unit correctly from the beginning.

This step ensures that every blood unit has a clear origin and can be traced later when needed.

### 2. Blood Unit Registration

Once the source is selected, the blood unit is added into the system.

- The unit is registered with blood group, component type, volume, and collection or received date.
- Storage details are recorded so the unit can be placed in the correct physical location.
- A unique unit reference is generated to identify the blood bag in the system.

This helps the team keep blood units organized and avoid manual tracking.

### 3. QR Assignment and Tracking

Each blood unit can be linked to a QR code for quick identification.

- The QR code is attached during blood unit creation.
- Staff can scan the QR code to identify the unit faster during daily operations.
- QR-based tracking helps reduce lookup time and improves accuracy when handling blood units.

This makes it easier to move between inventory, lab testing, and storage operations without confusion.

### 4. Screening and Testing

After a blood unit is registered, it moves into the screening workflow.

- The unit is marked as pending screening at the beginning.
- Lab staff record screening results for the mandatory tests.
- The unit status changes based on the test outcome.

Typical screening outcomes include:
- pending tests
- screening in progress
- screening safe
- quality check failure or other problem states

This step is important because only safe and approved units should continue into active inventory.

### 5. Storage Placement

After screening, the blood unit is stored in the correct equipment or storage location.

- The system records the building, zone, and equipment where the unit is kept.
- If a unit is moved later, the storage movement is tracked separately.
- Staff can always see where the unit is currently stored.

This keeps physical storage and digital tracking aligned.

### 6. Inventory Monitoring

The inventory view helps staff monitor available blood units across different blood groups.

- The dashboard shows stock summary and unit counts.
- Blood group cards provide a quick view of availability.
- Staff can open a blood group to see all related units in a list.

This allows the team to quickly understand stock position and act when a blood group is low or unavailable.

### 7. Reservation, Issue, and Return

When a blood unit is needed for a patient, it can move through reservation and issue workflows.

- A unit can be reserved for a specific request.
- A reserved unit can then be issued when required.
- If a unit is returned unused, it can be brought back into the workflow.
- Returned units can be marked for re-testing before reuse when needed.

This workflow helps the team manage actual hospital usage without losing track of the unit’s status.

### 8. Discard and Expiry Handling

Some units may not remain usable because of expiry, failed screening, damage, or other quality issues.

- The system supports discard handling with proper reason tracking.
- Expired or unusable units are kept separate from active inventory.
- Discarded units remain visible in the disposed view for audit and review.

This ensures unsafe or unusable units do not stay in the active stock list.

### 9. Movement and Audit History

Every important change is tracked in the system.

- Collection history is recorded.
- Screening history is recorded.
- Storage movement history is recorded separately.
- Issue, return, and discard actions are also tracked.

This gives staff a complete view of what happened to the unit over time.

### 10. Communication and Follow-Up

The system also supports communication-related follow-up for donors.

- Phone call history can be recorded.
- WhatsApp or other donor communication can be tracked.
- Staff can note donor responses, follow-up reminders, and remarks.

This helps the team maintain better donor engagement and future follow-up.

### 11. Settings and Master Data

Supporting values used throughout the system are managed through settings and master data.

- Collecting locations
- Storage locations
- Blood component types
- Discard reasons
- Other configurable system values

These master records help keep the workflow consistent and easy to manage.

### 12. Daily Operation Flow

In practice, the Blood Bank workflow usually follows this order:

- register or identify the source
- create the blood unit
- assign QR tracking
- screen and test the unit
- store the unit in the right location
- reserve or issue when required
- handle return, discard, or expiry when needed

This end-to-end flow helps staff manage blood bank operations in a clear and dependable way.

title: Diagrams
description: Add various diagram types, including flowcharts, decision trees and entity-relationship diagrams.
content:
Diagrams are powerful tools for visualizing processes, relationships, and decisions. This section showcases different types of diagrams created using **Mermaid**, complete with examples and reusable code snippets to integrate into your projects.

## Flowchart

A flowchart represents a sequence of steps or processes in a visual format. Use this diagram to map workflows, decision-making processes, or operational flows.

```jsx
<Mermaid chart="graph TD
Start --> Task1
Task1 --> Task2
Task2 --> End" />
```

## Decision Tree

Decision trees illustrate choices and possible outcomes, making them ideal for decision-making workflows or processes involving multiple paths.

```jsx
<Mermaid chart="graph TD
  A[Start] --> B{Is it raining?}
  B -->|Yes| C[Take an umbrella]
  B -->|No| D[Enjoy the weather]
  C --> E[Go outside]
  D --> E" 
/>
```

## Entity-Relationship Diagram

Entity-relationship diagrams (ERDs) are used to model relationships between entities in a system. They are widely used in database design and system architecture planning.

```jsx
<Mermaid chart="erDiagram
  CUSTOMER ||--o{ ORDER : places
  ORDER ||--|{ LINE-ITEM : contains
  PRODUCT ||--o{ LINE-ITEM : included in
  CUSTOMER {
    string name
    string email
  }
  ORDER {
    int orderNumber
    date orderDate
  }
  LINE-ITEM {
    int quantity
    float price
  }
  PRODUCT {
    int productId
    string name
    float price
  }" 
/>
```

Each of these diagrams serves a specific purpose and Mermaid makes it easy to generate them dynamically. Feel free to experiment with the provided code snippets and adapt them to your needs.

title: Filetree
description: This section provides an overview of file structures and their implementation using the FileTree component.
content:
This section demonstrates the structure of a file tree using the `FileTree` component. Below is an example showcasing folders and files organized hierarchically for a project setup.

## How to Use

Integrate the `FileTree` component into your project to visually represent file and folder structures. This is particularly useful for documentation, tutorials, or providing users with an overview of your project's architecture.

### JSX Code Example

Here is how you can define the file tree structure in for use in your project:

```jsx
<FileTree>
  <Folder name="src" label="Source Code">
    <File name="index.tsx" label="Index File" />
    <Folder name="components" label="Components">
      <File name="button.tsx" label="Button Component" />
      <File name="input.tsx" label="Input Component" />
    </Folder>
    <Folder name="pages" label="Pages">
      <File name="home.tsx" label="Home Page" />
      <File name="about.tsx" label="About Page" />
    </Folder>
  </Folder>
</FileTree>
```

Use this code as a template to set up your own file tree structure and customize it as needed.

The area of a circle ($$A$$) can be calculated using the radius ($$r$$) as follows:

```math
A = \pi r^2
```

## Quadratic Formula

The quadratic formula for solving an equation of the form $$ax^2 + bx + c = 0$$ is:

```math
x = \frac{-b \pm \sqrt{b^2 - 4ac}}{2a}
```

## Newton's Second Law of Motion

Newton's second law of motion states that force ($$F$$) is the product of mass ($$m$$) and acceleration ($$a$$):

```math
F = ma
```

## Pythagorean Theorem

The Pythagorean theorem relates the lengths of the sides of a right triangle:

```math
a^2 + b^2 = c^2
```

## Einstein's Mass-Energy Equivalence

Einstein's famous equation relates energy ($$E$$), mass ($$m$$), and the speed of light ($$c$$):

```math
E = mc^2
```
